tool.name: ProteinOrtho
tool.command: ## ProteinOrtho v6 creates its search databases and intermediate files next to the ## input FASTA files, therefore the inputs are symlinked into the working directory ## using a numbered naming scheme (0.fasta, 1.fasta, ...). #set $counter = 0 #for $f in $fasta_input: ln -s '${f}' '${counter}.fasta' && #set $counter = $counter + 1 #end for #if str($synteny.synteny_select) == '-synteny': #set $counter = 0 #for $g in $synteny.synteny_input: ln -s '${g}' '${counter}.gff' && #set $counter = $counter + 1 #end for #end if proteinortho -project=myproject -cpus=\$GALAXY_SLOTS $blast_type $compute_singles $compute_selfblast -e=$evalue_cutoff #if str($advanced.advanced_select) == 'advanced': -identity=$advanced.identity -cov=$advanced.coverage -conn=$advanced.connectivity -sim=$advanced.similarity -minspecies=$advanced.minspecies $advanced.core #end if #if str($synteny.synteny_select) == '-synteny': -synteny $synteny.synteny_dups -cs=$synteny.cs #set $counter = 0 #for $g in $synteny.synteny_input: '${counter}.gff' #set $counter = $counter + 1 #end for #end if #set $counter = 0 #for $f in $fasta_input: '${counter}.fasta' #set $counter = $counter + 1 #end for ## ProteinOrtho v6 writes all of its progress information to stderr, which Galaxy ## would flag as an error when using detect_errors="aggressive". Everything is ## therefore redirected into a log file that is returned as an additional output, ## so that only a non-zero exit code marks the job as failed. > '$logfile' 2>&1

param.name: fasta_input
param.label: FASTA files, one per species
param.help: Two or more FASTA files, each representing the protein (or gene) set of one species. Sequence identifiers must be unique within each file.

param.name: blast_type
param.label: Similarity search program
param.help: Alignment program used for the all-against-all comparison. DIAMOND is a fast alternative to BLASTP+ for amino acid sequences.

param.name: evalue_cutoff
param.label: E-value cutoff
param.help: Maximum E-value of a reported hit (default 1e-05).

param.name: compute_singles
param.label: Report singletons
param.help: Also report genes without any hit in the orthologous groups table.

param.name: compute_selfblast
param.label: Self-BLAST (detect direct paralogs)
param.help: Additionally performs a self comparison for each species to also detect paralogous genes without orthologs.

param.name: synteny_select
param.label: Synteny (PoFF) extension
param.help: Uses the gene order (GFF3 annotation) to separate similar sequences and to improve the orthology prediction.

param.name: synteny_input
param.label: GFF3 annotation files, one per species
param.help: One GFF3 file for each input FASTA file, given in the same order. Only rows of type CDS (column 3) are considered and column 9 must contain an attribute 'Name=GENE_IDENTIFIER' matching the FASTA identifier (no semicolons).

param.name: synteny_dups
param.label: Resolve duplicated regions
param.help: Enable the reiteration heuristic to determine duplicated regions (recommended when whole genome duplications are suspected).

param.name: cs
param.label: Size of a maximum common substring
param.help: Minimum size of a shared common substring (MCS) for adjacency matches in the PoFF algorithm (default 3).

param.name: advanced_select
param.label: Advanced clustering options
param.help: If set to 'Use advanced options' the similarity and clustering thresholds can be adjusted, otherwise the program defaults are used.

param.name: identity
param.label: Minimum percent identity of best hits
param.help: Minimum percent identity of the best search hits (default 25).

param.name: connectivity
param.label: Minimum algebraic connectivity
param.help: This is the main clustering parameter. Larger values result in more and smaller clusters. Use 0 to only compute connected components without splitting them, or -1 to skip the connectivity calculation (default 0.1).

param.name: similarity
param.label: Minimum reciprocal similarity
param.help: Minimum reciprocal similarity for additional hits (default 0.95). 1 reports only the best reciprocal hits, 0 reports all reciprocal hits within the other boundaries.

param.name: minspecies
param.label: Minimum species per group
param.help: Orthologous groups that contain less than this number of species are not split any further (default 1).

param.name: core
param.label: Core genes only
param.help: Only report orthologous groups that span all species. Overrules the connectivity parameter.

tool.help:
ProteinOrtho ============
ProteinOrtho is a tool to detect (co-)orthologous genes within different species. It performs an all-against-all similarity comparison of the input FASTA files and partitions the resulting similarity graph into orthologous gene groups. The PoFF (Protein Family Finder) extension additionally uses the gene order (synteny) to separate similar sequences.
----- Input -----
Two or more FASTA files, one for each species. The files may either contain amino acid or nucleotide sequences, but all files must be of the same type and must be matched with the corresponding similarity search program. Sequence identifiers must be unique within each file.
------ Output ------
**Orthologous groups** (`myproject.proteinortho.tsv`)
A tabular file with one row per orthologous group:
- Column 1: number of species in the group - Column 2: number of genes in the group - Column 3: algebraic connectivity of the group. The group is split when the connectivity falls below the given threshold (`-conn`, default 0.1). A value of 1 means the group is fully connected. - One column per input species with the identifiers of the genes of the group. Species that are absent from a group are marked with `*`. Multiple genes of one species within a group (co-orthologs / paralogs) are separated by commas.
**Relation graph** (`myproject.proteinortho-graph`)
A pairwise list of the relations between all genes of the input files (`geneA geneB evalue_ab bitscore_ab evalue_ba bitscore_ba`).
With the synteny extension the additional files `myproject.poff.tsv` and `myproject.poff-graph` are generated, in which the adjacency information is combined with the sequence similarity.
------ Synteny ------
The PoFF extension requires a GFF3 annotation file for each input FASTA file (in the same order). Only rows of type `CDS` (column 3) are considered. Column 9 must contain the attribute `Name=GENE_IDENTIFIER`, where the gene identifier must match the identifier used in the FASTA file. Semicolons must not be used in the attributes.
----- Options -------
- **E-value cutoff**: maximum E-value of a reported hit (default 1e-05) - **Minimum percent identity**: default 25 - **Minimum coverage**: default 50 - **Minimum algebraic connectivity**: the main clustering parameter, default 0.1 - **Minimum reciprocal similarity**: default 0.95 - **Report singletons**: also report genes without any hit - **Self-BLAST**: detect paralogous genes without orthologs
